One mind alone can want, but cannot sing
a word needs air that many lungs permit.
So angels lend a voice, and giving fling
ten heaven bells silver, make echoes sing.

We pass the pen like heat from palm to palm,
each letter lifted from someone's name. Yet
No single writer signs the finished psalm;
the many made it, so the many claim.

And once the final line is sealed and still,
what speaks is not the whole but something more:
a self no single self could yet fulfill,
a melody no tongue can house, a score.

The poem is a lantern passed, not planned;
no single hand could make the meaning stand."}
